solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Reported description of Trotsky's assassin?

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the phrase counts, not its spelling

parts.note: Trotsky was a follower of Karl Marx, so he could be described as a Marx man

explanation.surface: A newspaper asking how the man who killed Trotsky was described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as one definition, but 'assassin' alone defines MARKSMAN; 'description of Trotsky's' is the Marxist label MARX MAN, spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A marksman is a skilled shooter, the kind of person hired as an assassin.

clue.text: Sweetly thick sort of male seen with old girls

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for male
o is the abbreviation for old
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: A dim but charming man going out with former schoolgirls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetly thick sort' looks like a description of a nice but dim man; it is a syrup that is sweet and thick.
explanation.definitionFit: Molasses is the dark, sticky syrup left from sugar refining, both sweet and very viscous.

clue.text: Ordinary men can be offensive as well as row

parts.note: rank means foul-smelling, offensive
and means as well as
a file is a line or row, as in single file

explanation.surface: Ordinary men can be both aggressive and quarrelsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' and 'row' pull towards fighting; here they mean smelly and a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank and file are the ordinary soldiers or members, as opposed to officers or leaders.

clue.text: Tired and in bits?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: exhausted, in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone worn out and emotionally falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both utterly exhausted in informal speech and literally broken into many pieces.

clue.text: A fellow extremely angry right-wing leaders frighten

parts.note: taken as written
f is the abbreviation for fellow

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so only the first letter of each of the words before is taken

parts.note: the first letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A furious right-wing chap scaring the party's leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: Afear is an archaic verb, found in Shakespeare's era, related to the familiar adjective afeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To afear someone is an old word for making them afraid, the same as scaring them.

clue.text: Professional able to make an excess of revenue

parts.note: the usual short form of professional
fit means able or suitable, as in fit to work

explanation.surface: A competent professional who can make more money than they spend.
explanation.definitionFit: Profit is the surplus left when income exceeds costs, so it is an excess of revenue.

clue.text: Game of cards is rotten when you have no clubs

indicators.note: having none of something means it is gone, so that letter drops out

parts.note: crummy means poor or rotten
C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A card game is no fun when your hand holds no clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a popular card game in which players collect sets and runs.

clue.text: Porky female seen with one heading for bakery

parts.note: f is the abbreviation for female
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, so only its first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter of bakery

explanation.surface: A plump woman and a friend making for the bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porky' looks like an insult about weight; it is rhyming slang, porky pie meaning lie.
explanation.definitionFit: A porky, from the rhyming slang porky pie, is a lie, and a fib is a small lie.

clue.text: Vehicles with on-board computers rolled over

indicators.note: a thing rolled over ends up upside down, so the word runs the opposite way in this down light

parts.note: smart devices have built-in computing, as in smartphone

explanation.surface: Self-driving cars that crashed and overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are rail vehicles running along street tracks carrying passengers.

clue.text: Where one might see Edinburgh comic break?

definitions.text: Where one might see Edinburgh comic
definitions.note: a cryptic phrase read as two words, in Fringe
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a comedian performs at the Edinburgh Festival Fringe, so you see them at that event
second meaning: to violate a rule or a right

explanation.walkthrough: The Edinburgh Festival Fringe is the huge open-access arts festival held every August, famous for stand-up comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a law or patent is to break or violate it.

clue.text: Ancestry series gets silver medal (that's only 2nd place!)

parts.note: a line is a series, as in a line of kings
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: only the thing in second place is kept, meaning just the second letter of the word before

parts.note: the second letter of medal

explanation.surface: A dynasty that wins only silver, joking that second place is all it manages.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a rueful aside about silver, but it is an instruction to take the second letter of 'medal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineage is a line of descent from forebears, which is exactly what ancestry means.

clue.text: Guy going about island without bit of sleep is a state

indicators.note: to go about is to turn round, so the word for guy is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a guy is a man

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the island must lose the letter named next

parts.note: the Spanish Balearic island
Z, as in catching some zs, stands for a little sleep

explanation.surface: A sleepless party-goer touring Ibiza, worn out in a bit of a state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is a state' reads like a comment on the tired man, but 'a state' is the definition: a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is an independent country in south-west Africa, and a country is a sovereign state.

clue.text: Broadcaster in streetcar travelling around

indicators.note: letters that travel around move from their places and end up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A radio presenter riding a tram around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcaster' suggests radio or television, but here it is the old farming sense of someone who sows seed by flinging it widely.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast seed is to scatter it by hand, so one who broadcasts in that sense is a scatterer.

clue.text: I'm alarmed if president punches Yankee and son

indicators.note: a punch drives into something, so the president's name is pushed inside the other letters

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Ike was the nickname of US President Dwight Eisenhower
s is the abbreviation for son in family trees

explanation.surface: A shocked onlooker watching a president throw punches at an American and his son.
explanation.definitionFit: Yikes is an exclamation of sudden fright, the word someone blurts when alarmed.

clue.text: Cause of complaint doctor in Keys noted

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor in the Florida Keys records why a patient is unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' in a medical sense means an ailment, not a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidney stone is a hard mineral deposit in the kidney and a well-known cause of painful illness.

clue.text: One downed wine that's brought over

indicators.note: bringing something over flips it, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: red is a wine
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone who knocked back a glass of wine that a waiter carried across.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Downed' suggests drinking; here it means covered in down. The eider is a sea duck prized for its soft breast feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider duck lines its nest with fine down feathers, the source of eiderdown, so it is a bird with down.

clue.text: Jet or blue ribbed fabric on back of costume

parts.note: blue is the colour of the Conservative party, so blue means Tory, shortened to Con
cord, or corduroy, is a ribbed cloth

indicators.note: the back of a word is where it ends, so only its final letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of costume

explanation.surface: Choosing between a black or blue corduroy fabric for the back of an outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jet' and 'blue' both look like colours, but 'Jet' is the aircraft. Blue for Conservative is a British political convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Concorde was the Anglo-French supersonic airliner, a jet-powered passenger aircraft.

clue.text: Bubbly title-holders embracing old head of state

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap one's arms round, so one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: champs, short for champions, hold titles
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: Champions celebrating with fizz while hugging a former monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Bubbly and champers are both informal names for champagne.

clue.text: American monk with a halo in need of adjustment

indicators.note: something needing adjustment is out of position, so the letters must be put into a new order

parts.note: the letters of monk, a and halo

explanation.surface: A US monk whose halo has slipped and wants straightening.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oklahoman is a native of Oklahoma, a US state, so is an American.

clue.text: Awful boss eats stuff that is bad for you

definitions.text: stuff that is bad for you

indicators.note: something awful is in a terrible state, so the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A dreadful manager eating junk food.
explanation.definitionFit: Asbestos is a fibrous mineral whose dust causes serious lung disease, a hazardous material.

clue.text: A pen that might be seen around a cob?

definitions.text: A pen that might be seen around a cob?

parts.note: surface reading: a pen is a female swan, so this seems to describe a female swan swimming near a male one, a cob
setter's reading: a pen is also an enclosure, and one built to go around a bird such as a cob

explanation.walkthrough: Pen and cob are the names for female and male swans, which pulls the solver to the riverbank; the pen is an enclosure, and the cob merely a bird kept in it.
explanation.definitionFit: A cage for keeping birds is a small enclosure, a kind of pen made to hold any bird.

clue.text: City stars needing to make a break in the centre

indicators.note: the single letter a is needed to become something else, so it is swapped out

parts.note: the leads are the stars of a film or show

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, the only one kept

parts.note: the middle letter of break

explanation.surface: Football stars needing to make a breakthrough down the middle, Leeds United perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: Read it as: stars needing to make the letter A into the centre of 'break'. The A in LEADS becomes E.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Dope smuggled by a model-type and actor

indicators.note: smuggled goods are carried hidden inside, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: taken as written
dope and gen both mean inside information
the Model T was Ford's famous early car

explanation.surface: Drugs smuggled by a fashion model and a stage actor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Actor' suggests a stage performer, but here it means simply one who acts, often on behalf of another.
explanation.definitionFit: An agent is someone who acts or brings about an effect, so the word is a synonym for a doer.

clue.text: Fish hang loosely after end of rod is removed

indicators.note: removing something takes it away, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: to dangle is to hang loosely

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, the one picked out

parts.note: the last letter of rod

explanation.surface: An angler's line hanging slack after the tip of the rod snaps off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with rod, line and hook.

clue.text: Tense, good man taking off close to rivers could be Sully

parts.note: t is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so a letter goes

parts.note: a saint is a very good person

indicators.note: the close of a word is its last letter, which is the one chosen

parts.note: the last letter of rivers

explanation.surface: A tense hero landing on a river, Sully being the pilot who ditched in the Hudson.
explanation.walkthrough: Sully, Captain Sullenberger, landed a plane on the Hudson; here 'Sully' is the verb to soil.
explanation.definitionFit: To taint is to contaminate or spoil the purity of something, as sully does.

clue.text: PDC primarily broadcast a set shot at the double

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the first letter of PDC
these eight letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Darts commentary on a set shot at a double, the PDC being the Professional Darts Corporation.
explanation.walkthrough: In darts the double is the outer ring that doubles a score; here 'at the double' is the idiom for very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Posthaste means with great speed, as does the military idiom at the double.

clue.text: Some mafioso chilling in a Russian city

indicators.note: some means only part of what follows, so the letters sit within the phrase

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A mobster relaxing on holiday in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Sochi is a Black Sea resort in Russia, host of the 2014 Winter Olympics.

clue.text: One installing Windows in Gulf's more idle

parts.note: G is the standard abbreviation for gulf on maps, as in G. of Mexico
lazier means more idle

explanation.surface: An IT technician setting up Microsoft Windows somewhere in the Gulf who is lazier than most.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital W points to the software; the windows here are panes of glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a tradesperson who fits glass into window frames.

clue.text: Craft seen by planet without wings

indicators.note: wings are at the sides, so having none means both outermost letters go

parts.note: Earth is our planet

explanation.surface: A spacecraft without wings spotted near a planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a vessel, beside planet and wings, but it means skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Art and craft both mean skill gained through practice, as in the art of persuasion.

clue.text: Company by motorway stronghold gets relief

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
M is used for British motorways, as in the M1
a fort is a stronghold

explanation.surface: A firm whose castle beside the motorway gets planning relief.
explanation.definitionFit: Comfort is the easing of grief or pain, which is what relief means.

clue.text: Property in Spain controlled by the government

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
the state is the government of a country

explanation.surface: A country house in Spain that the government owns.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate is a large piece of land or the whole of someone's assets, both kinds of property.

clue.text: Those in van in repose must be whacked

indicators.note: whacked things are knocked about out of shape, so the letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: People resting in a van who are about to get beaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: Van here is the vanguard, the front of an advance, not a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneers are the first to go somewhere new, the people at the front of any movement.
